title: Civil status and spouse data
purpose: Ask for civil status and, where the fund requires it, the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth. Map civil status to the pension fund's list and to the source tax groups.

stories.title: Ask every employee for their civil status
stories.i_want: every new employee to state their civil status, choosing from Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership or Separated
stories.so_that: the required 'Civil status' field of the registration can be filled and source tax can tell the married path from the single path, without HR having to ask the employee again
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration, and the source tax tariff code depends on it. Without it, both the registration and the tariff code are blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their residence, nationality or source tax situation
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked, and the employee cannot submit the questionnaire without answering it

acceptance_criteria.title: Exactly six civil status options
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The first four are the pension fund's own list, written as the fund writes them. Registered partnership and Separated are added so that the calculator's groups can be answered and employees such as Daniel, who is in a registered partnership, can answer truthfully. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: offering these two extra options and mapping them as described in the stories on civil status for the pension fund and for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives the civil status
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is recorded for the pension fund registration (as the fund's civil status) and for the source tax tariff determination (as the calculator's civil status group). The employee is not asked for their civil status a second time for either party.

stories.title: Ask for the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth when the fund registers the employee as Married
stories.i_want: the date of birth of the spouse or registered partner of every employee who is married, in a registered partnership or separated
stories.so_that: the registration is not blocked, because the fund requires the spouse's date of birth whenever the civil status entered is Married
stories.priority_reason: The fund blocks registration of a married employee without the spouse's date of birth ('Spouse's date of birth is required.'), and HR names this as missing data today.

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked and required for married, registered-partnership and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered that their civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their spouse's or registered partner's date of birth and cannot submit without it. Married is confirmed by HR and the fund. Registered partnership and Separated are both entered at the fund as Married, so the fund requires the date there too. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: that the fund accepts a registered partnership and a separation entered as Married with this date of birth.

acceptance_criteria.title: Not asked for single, divorced or widowed employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered that their civil status is Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.then: they are not asked for a spouse's or partner's date of birth, and no spouse data goes to the pension fund for them. The fund shows the field only for Married. No screenshot shows the form for Divorced or Widowed, so not asking here is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

acceptance_criteria.title: Form and recipient of the spouse's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their spouse's or registered partner's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is entered as DD.MM.YYYY (for example 14.03.1988), as the fund requires, and is recorded only for the pension fund registration, as the fund's 'Spouse's date of birth'. No other receiving party gets it.

acceptance_criteria.title: A date of birth that no longer applies is not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changed their civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth they entered earlier is discarded and goes to no party. If they switch back before submitting, the earlier entry may still be shown, so no input is lost.

stories.title: Answer the calculator's civil status question from the employee's civil status
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status turned into the calculator's two groups: 'married or registered partnership' and 'single, divorced, separated or widowed'
stories.so_that: Lonio can follow the married or single path of the Zurich calculator when it computes the tariff code, without asking the employee a second civil status question
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the full tariff code instead of HR (D-001). The calculator's civil status decides the married or single path, the spouse questions and the tariff letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married and registered partnership count as married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is 'Married or registered partnership', as in the calculator's own group

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, divorced, separated and widowed count as single
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is 'Single, divorced, separated or widowed', as in the calculator's own group. A separated employee counts as single for source tax, even though the pension fund registers them as Married.

acceptance_criteria.title: A registered partner counts as a spouse wherever source tax looks at the spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the employee is subject to source tax and computes the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the registered partner is treated like a spouse. This includes the exemption for employees married to a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland, and the spouse questions on the married path, as the calculator groups registered partnership with married.

acceptance_criteria.title: Always derived from the latest answer
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is changed after submission (by HR, for example after a marriage)
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for source tax is needed again
acceptance_criteria.then: it is derived again from the latest civil status. The earlier result is not kept.

stories.title: Enter the civil status on the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status expressed as one of my four values: Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
stories.so_that: every employee can be registered, including registered partners and separated employees, whose status is not on my list
stories.priority_reason: The fund's civil status field is required and offers only four values. Without a mapping, a registered partner such as Daniel or a separated employee cannot be registered, and HR does not know what the fund wants in that case.

acceptance_criteria.title: Statuses on the fund's list are entered unchanged
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: the fund gets the same civil status the employee gave

acceptance_criteria.title: Registered partnership and separated are entered as Married
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: the fund gets Married, together with the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth that the employee gave. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: HR does not know how the fund handles a registered partnership, and the fund's list has neither status.

acceptance_criteria.title: Always derived from the latest answer
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's civil status is changed after submission (by HR, for example after a marriage or a separation)
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status for the pension fund is needed again
acceptance_criteria.then: it is derived again from the latest civil status
